Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. As we go through the written RFP, we've got a few detailed follow-up questions to validate compliance for our EU retail banking workloads (high sensitivity PII). Please confirm the following for inclusion in our procurement pack: 

1) Which physical regions do you offer for production data residency (control plane + persisted customer data) in EU, US, and APAC? Please be specific to availability zones/regions — we need to map to our internal controls.

2) Do you support automatic cross-border failover (e.g., EU->US) for high-availability? If so, what contractual controls are required and what data processing flows change during failover?

3) For backups and cold storage snapshots, where are those stored by default? Can customers restrict backup storage to the same country as production?

4) Key management: do you offer customer-managed keys (BYOK) across all deployment types (hosted, dedicated, private)? Any HSM/KMS limitations per region?

5) Evidence: SOC 2/ISO/other certs, and a short statement about audit log retention and access for customers in the EU.

If you can send a short, authoritative set of answers and any appendices we can include in the RFP, that would be ideal. We may ask for a proposed contractual clause for cross-border replication options.

Regards,

Subject: RE: RFP Q12 — data residency / cross-border failover

Hi Nadia —

Thanks for the clear questions. Please find concise answers below for your RFP entry; attached is a technical appendix (redwood-data-residency-appendix.pdf) and a region-to-ISO mapping workbook. Let me know if you'd like a single-page summary for procurement.

1) Regions (production data residency):
- EU: Primary options — eu-central-1 (Frankfurt), eu-west-1 (Dublin). We also offer eu-west-3 (Paris) in Dedicated/Private deployments on request and through partnership regions.
- US: us-east-1 (N. Virginia), us-west-2 (Oregon).
- APAC: ap-southeast-1 (Singapore), ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo).
Notes: All hosted regions are operated from our managed clusters; customers can request region pinning per project. The attached spreadsheet lists AZ-level mappings and expected network egress points.

2) Cross-border failover:
- Automatic cross-border failover is supported only as an opt-in configuration and is considered a DR feature, not the default.
- By default, traffic and persisted customer data remain within the chosen residency region. Cross-border failover requires: (a) a contractual amendment to the DPA specifying permitted jurisdictions for replicated data; (b) customer opt-in at deployment time; and (c) explicit configuration of replication windows and retention policies.
- During failover, write operations are routed to the active region and transient read replicas may be spun up in the DR region. All replicated data is encrypted in transit and at rest using the configured KMS keys. We do not perform any unilateral cross-border replication for production workloads without contractual permission.

3) Backups / snapshots:
- Default: snapshots and backups for hosted customers are stored in the same cloud region by default.
- Restriction: For EU customers, we support an option to restrict backup storage to the same country or EU region in our Hosted offering, subject to configuration and acceptable cost/latency tradeoffs. This is available for Dedicated and Private deployments by design.

4) Key management:
- Hosted: We support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed KMS (BYOK) via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault) in all primary regions listed. For EU regions, BYOK requires a key in the same cloud region; bring-your-own-HSM (PKCS#11) options are available for Dedicated and Private customers.
- Dedicated/Private: Full support for customer-managed HSMs and on-prem KMS with customer-controlled keys.
- Limitations: HSM appliance procurement and cross-region key replication are customer-managed for private deployments; Redwood can provide integration support but does not host customer HSM keys for on-prem deployments.

5) Evidence / audits:
- Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications (scope documents attached).
- Audit logs: Control-plane and per-request audit logs are retained for 1 year by default for Hosted customers; retention can be extended for Dedicated/Private deployments per contract. Customers can request log exports for their own SIEM. Access to audit logs requires appropriate admin roles and is subject to data access controls in the DPA.

Operational notes that often matter to banks:
- Data deletion: upon contract termination or project decommissioning, we provide a documented workflow for secure deletion of persisted customer data and retention of anonymized telemetry, subject to the agreed retention schedule in the DPA.
- Data processing locations: metadata required for routing (e.g., IPs, health checks) may transit through our control plane; control-plane metadata collection is described in the appendix.

I've attached the region mapping and the residency appendix. If you want, we can propose a short clause for the DPA that states the conditions under which cross-border replication is permitted (I can draft that and loop in Laura for legal sign-off).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Marissa / Vivek —

Thanks for the draft. A few legal points to tighten before we send to Orange Bank: 
- "Opt-in" for cross-border failover must be accompanied by (i) permitted jurisdictions list in the DPA, (ii) explicit customer authorization for replication at the project level, and (iii) a defined maximum failover duration beyond which data must be quarantined or deleted in the DR region.
- Add a clause that backups will not be moved outside of the agreed residency region unless customer signs a specific addendum.
- For BYOK, we should clarify responsibility for key compromise: customer controls keys and is responsible for key security; Redwood will not have access to customer-managed keys. Add language describing key-rotation support windows.

I'll prepare a redline (proposed-rfp-redlines-v1.docx) and a single-paragraph summary for procurement. We should also include our SOC 2 Type II date range and a contact for sharing the SOC report under NDA.

Legal notes: Cross-border replication requires (1) customer opt-in and project-level authorization, (2) DPA amendment specifying permitted jurisdictions and replication retention, and (3) predefined failover windows and post-failover remediation/quarantine processes. Details are in the attached DPA redline.
